title: How logging in works
subtitle: from the password box to a session

steps.title: It starts with you
steps.say: You type your email and password into the login form. Nothing has left your browser yet.

steps.title: The request
steps.say: The web app sends both to the **Auth API** in one `POST /login` request.

steps.title: Is it really you?
steps.say: The API loads your row from Postgres and compares **password hashes**. The real password is never stored.

steps.title: Remember the visit
steps.say: If the hash matches, the API creates a session id and keeps it in Redis, so later requests are cheap to check.

steps.title: The answer
steps.say: The browser gets the session id back as a cookie. From now on every request carries it.

notes.text: httpOnly cookie: JS can't read it

steps.title: The whole trip
steps.say: Four hops: **send**, **check**, **remember**, **answer**. A wrong password stops the trip at step 2.
